short: 39-phoneme decoding from dorsal Utah arrays (M06) and overt-speech confound controls (M12) are standard: both have read priors, T5 alone carries them, and folds share words.
position: The paper [@wilson2020decoding] changes two components, and both are standard. The decoder (M06) extends the same group's 10- and 11-class syllable and word decoding from the same participant and arrays [@stavisky2019neural] to 39 phonemes, but the full inventory had already been classified from intracortical [@brumberg2011classification] and ECoG [@mugler2014direct] signals, and the authors' matched test lands at the ECoG level: 36.8% against 36.1% on consonants. The evaluation (M12) adds overt-speech confound controls that no prior decoder with full text in the Appendix population applies, but the contamination test and its decoding consequence come from Roussel et al. [@roussel2020observation], whom the authors credit, and every control runs in T5 alone. The strongest confound is the split: utterance-level folds over three repetitions of each of 420 words let test phonemes share words, and context, with training (inference from Secs. 2.2, 3.2). The authors' own judgment that two dorsal arrays are insufficient for fluent open-vocabulary communication (Sec. 4) holds; "competitive" with ECoG holds only as the ballpark estimate they call it (Sec. 4.1).
